(1) the health of older persons is a function of the interplay of biological and psychosocial factors; (2) the effects of these factors are moderated by individual differences and by the environment; (3) health is a multidimensional phenomenon that includes biological, psychological, and social components; (4) the health of individuals is influenced by their health beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors; and (5) the health of the older population can be improved by the application of health promotion and disease

(1) health and behavior are inextricably linked, (2) health and behavior change over the life span and are related to the context in which they occur, (3) health and behavior interact with each other and with other variables, and (4) health and behavior influence each other.

health, behavior, behavior change, and aging are all inextricably linked and that a life span perspective on aging and health is critical to understanding how and why older persons live the way they do.
